articles.title: Durham v Gloucestershire, Glamorgan v Hampshire: county cricket, day three – live
articles.summary: County Championship updates | England v Pakistan live Day two roundup | Sign up for the Spin | Mail Tanya. Lunch at 1.10. Everyone out in the middle practising and the groundstaff are sanding (? )the outfield. Remaining cloudy this afternoon.
body: Rain rudely interrupted the County Championship on bank holiday Saturday but there was evening controversy at Chester-le-Street. Kasey Aldridge had bowled Durham to almost-victory with four for 47, giving him nine wickets in the match, leaving his side four to win. But with the floodlights on and filthy skies, Gloucestershire refused to bowl spin and the umpires said it was too dark for pace.

Mark Alleyne, the Gloucestershire head coach, explained: “Forty-five minutes before we lost the last wicket, it was too dark to play, which would have been consistent with all the other days that we played.

“I was really surprised that Carse was allowed to bowl to [James] Bracey at the time. He got him out, then took off straight away. So, yeah, we had probably 50 minutes of cricket there that we probably shouldn’t have done.
“They asked if we would bowl our spinners to finish the game. Of course, we said: ‘No, we’ll bowl our quick bowlers,’ in which case it became bad light, so we’ll come back tomorrow.

articles.title: Maguire fires superb 63 as Alexander lead cut at Irish Open
articles.summary: Ireland's Leona Maguire fires a superb nine-under-par 63 at the Women's Irish Open at the K Club in County Kildare as Casandra Alexander leads by three going into Sunday's final round.
body: Ireland's Leona Maguire delighted the home crowd by shooting a superb nine-under-par 63 on day three of the Women's Irish Open at the K Club to sit seven shots behind leader Casandra Alexander.
Maguire birdied nine of the first 15 holes in a bogey-free round to lie in a tie for sixth position on 11 under.
Her birdie putt on the 18th for a 62 lipped out but the Cavan native will be happy to have returned to her best form after two opening rounds of 71.
Maguire picked up shots on successive holes between the second and the fourth, with further back-to-back birdies coming on the seventh and eighth as she posted 31 shots for her outward nine.

articles.title: Elanga and Wissa strike as Newcastle extends Spurs’ miserable start to season
articles.summary: If ever you wanted to understand the distinction between ‘winning the transfer market’ and winning an actual football match, then this was the game for you. Tottenham’s first home fixture of the Premier League season began with adulatory focus on all their new players.
body: Tottenham should have taken the lead in a first half they had the better of, but they had no response to impressive second-half strikes by Anthony Elanga and Yoanne Wissa. What had looked like green shoots of positivity withered to nothing. For a Newcastle team themselves a work in progress under Matthias Jaissle, this was a heartening victory achieved with many of their own additions to come in.

Rarely can there have been a club so desperate to show their fans that they have flashed the cash as Spurs this summer. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive, wrote a two-page letter in the programme that led on the spending and proclaimed: “We have attracted the names we wanted to attract.” Before kick-off there was a brief ceremony to welcome all eight signings to the club. “We spent and we spent, and we’ve got lots of top players,” sang the club announcer.

articles.title: Moyes says Everton must keep best players after Forest bid for Harrison Armstrong
articles.summary: ‘I don’t think we can afford to lose any players’ Nottingham Forest reportedly make £40m offer. The sale of the 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest would be a “club decision” for Everton, according to David Moyes.
body: “I know there’s been an offer, I don’t really think there’s much else I’ve got to say about it,” Moyes said, initially refusing to be drawn. “It’s not really a question for just now, it’ll be a club decision.”

Moyes has previously suggested his discomfort with a lack of business this summer, suggesting his squad was not big enough. His stance was unaltered here on Saturday. “I have said we could do with strengthening and hopefully we can do that. We have a good basis. Let’s hope we can build on it.
“I don’t think we can afford to lose any players, certainly not our better ones. The club dictates a lot of that and we will see how the next few days go.”
Travelling Everton fans sang that the club would have a “riot on your hands” should Armstrong be sold. Moyes, when asked about the supporters’ reaction, said: “I’d say the manager’s an Evertonian.”

articles.title: South Africa hold off All Blacks fightback to level series
articles.summary: World champions South Africa deliver a powerful first-half performance as they edge past New Zealand and level 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' series at 1-1.
body: World champions South Africa delivered a powerful first-half performance as they edged past New Zealand and levelled 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' series at 1-1 with two Tests to play.
The All Blacks travelled to Cape Town knowing a win would write them into the history books as the first New Zealand team to win back-to-back Tests in South Africa since the 'Incomparables' of 1996.
But South Africa dominated the basics and showed a more clinical edge this week, even though the lively All Blacks again outscored them on the try count by four to three.

New Zealand's fightback ultimately came too late, captain Ardie Savea barging over on 77 minutes to get the game within a score, but on the All Blacks' final attack Boks replacement Cameron Hanekom won a superb turnover that settled the nervy closing stages.

articles.title: Carson Schwesinger 'ready to roll' for Browns after training camp injury
articles.summary: Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger missed a large percentage of training camp with an undisclosed injury. He finally returned to the field Aug. 29.
body: BEREA ― Carson Schwesinger is on a need-to-know basis when it comes to the injury that kept him out of nearly four weeks' worth of training camp. As far as the Browns linebacker is concerned, if you're not one of his coaches or teammates, you don't need to know.
"I mean, it's just football," Schwesinger said prior to practice Aug. 29. "Sometimes things happen and you got to try and be smart about it. That's basically it. I'm ready to roll now."
Schwesinger missed his first practice Aug. 1. He finally returned to the practice field in full team drills Aug. 29.

The 2025 Defensive Rookie of the Year never showed any obvious signs of a specific injury throughout his absence. He was routinely witnessed doing various drills, be it running or pushing/pulling sleds of weight, between the team's walkthrough and their practice during camp.

articles.title: Henshaw wins world gold 11 days after being in hospital
articles.summary: Britain's Charlotte Henshaw has won her 12th Para-canoe World Championship title - less than two weeks after being in hospital with cellulitis.
body: The 39-year-old contracted the condition - usually a bacterial infection which makes the skin painful, hot and swollen - in her leg and, after leaving hospital, was unable to train on the water in the lead up to the championships in Poznan, Poland.

But in Saturday's KL2 200m final she crossed the finish line more than three seconds ahead of the rest of the field for her eighth world title in the event, adding to the four she has won in the VL3 equivalent.
"Of all the titles I've managed to win, that probably means the most because I did not know I was going to be here a week ago," she said.
"There's maybe something to be said for taking the pressure off and going out and trusting my body and my experience.

articles.title: What's behind Newcastle's hot start? Matthias Jaissle is 'Newcastle's best signing' according to Yoane Wissa
articles.summary: Even the most optimistic Newcastle United supporters were unlikely to have said Matthias Jaissle's team would come away from this start to the season with four points, but here are the Magpies anyway.
body: They can't be the surprise of the season given Hull City are 2-0, but Jaissle has walked into the shoes of a living club legend and found a way to a draw with Liverpool and a win over Tottenham Hotspur.

How did he do it? A perfect storm, you might say. Jaissle has taken sandpaper to the edges of perceived square pegs in round holes while getting instant magic from at least two of the club's signings made in the wake of Newcastle selling Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, and Sandro Tonali.

Surely, there's a siege mentality here, too, as well as a heaping helping of luck and the fact that Jaissle wouldn't have to do much but point at the massive opposition over the first two weeks as town-skippers Alexander Isak and Tonali started each outing on the other side of the pitch.

The Magpies saw goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek and Amar Dedic debut against Liverpool as two of the better players on the pitch, then deliver repeat performances while Nico Gonzalez joined them as a brilliant black and white debutant in Week 2.

articles.title: 'A joke!' - Hussain fumes as day three at Lord's abandoned amid sunshine
articles.summary: A seething Nasser Hussain said the umpires' decision to abandon play late on day three of the second Test between England and Pakistan was "a joke".
body: Just 24.5 overs were possible on a gloomy Saturday due to rain and bad light, during which time England moved from their overnight 81-3 to 177-7 for a lead of 357 as they look to wrap up a series win.

There looked to be a chance of more cricket when the sun began to shine late in the evening, only for the day to be officially called off just after 6.30pm local time, prompting heavy booing from spectators.
Had the players returned to the field before 7pm, play could have been extended to 7.30pm.
On hearing news of the abandonment, Sky Sports expert Hussain said: "That's a joke, honestly a joke. That is an unbelievable decision, it really is.

articles.title: Spurs beaten again as Elanga and Wissa strike for Newcastle
articles.summary: Tottenham have lost their first two Premier League matches and failed to score in both as rejuvenated duo Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa struck to earn Newcastle a 2-0 victory.
body: Spurs' big-spending summer, in which they have splashed £320m on eight new players, is yet to have an impact on Roberto De Zerbi's side, who were booed off a week on from being thrashed 3-0 at Brentford and lacked a cutting edge in their first home league game despite handing a debut to forward Omar Marmoush.

De Zerbi's other key signing, £75m winger Savio, has already been dealt an injury blow, missing out with "muscle fatigue", while midfielder Sandro Tonali, who left Newcastle in a £100m move, was mocked by his former supporters as they collected their first win.

Tottenham were the better side in the first half, with Newcastle goalkeeper Lucas Hornicek making saves from Mathys Tel and Jan Paul van Hecke, but Elanga, who struggled last season but shone last weekend with a goal against Liverpool, swivelled in the area and sent a shot off the post midway through the second half to put Newcastle ahead.

articles.title: Kolbe stars, Kolisi returns to XV as Springboks level series with New Zealand
articles.summary: South Africa roared back into Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry as returning captain Siya Kolisi marked his comeback with a try in a thrilling 33-26 victory over New Zealand in Cape Town, levelling the four-Test series at 1-1.
body: The sides shared seven tries, with Jesse Kriel, Damian de Allende and Kolisi crossing for the Springboks, either side of scores from Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie and Leroy Carter. But Cheslin Kolbe's 18 points from the tee ultimately proved decisive.

All Blacks captain Ardie Savea added a late fourth try for New Zealand - his 33rd in Test rugby - as the visitors finished with four tries to South Africa's three, but they were unable to overcome Kolbe's flawless accuracy.

Savea had predicted before kick-off that New Zealand would face a "wounded beast", and South Africa delivered an immediate response. Kriel crossed inside the opening two minutes, only for Roigard to hit back midway through a breathless opening quarter.

Kolbe's first penalty and de Allende's try either side of the 20-minute mark reasserted South African control. McKenzie's converted score kept the All Blacks within touching distance, but Kolisi crashed over on the stroke of half-time to send the hosts into the break with a 24-14 lead.
